shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: Only floating elements that cover content: toasts, menus, dialogs.

motion.name: print
motion.purpose: The tape strip printing out, the only thing that moves on its own.

components.name: Tape Strip
components.description: Printed label tape for ticket IDs, the product name and the rank.
components.css: .ds-tape { display: inline-block; padding: var(--space-1) var(--space-2); background: var(--color-tape-primary); color: var(--color-tape-ink); font-family: var(--font-tape); font-size: var(--text-tape-size); font-weight: var(--font-weight-strong); line-height: var(--text-tape-leading); letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; clip-path: polygon(4px 0, 100% 0, calc(100% - 4px) 100%, 0 100%); }

components.name: Cable Tab
components.description: A side panel tab with the 3 px cable run of its kind of work.
components.css: .ds-tab { padding: var(--space-2) var(--space-3); background: var(--color-surface-panel); color: var(--color-text-muted); border: 0; border-top: var(--border-width-cable) solid var(--color-cable-ticket); border-radius: var(--radius-corner); font-family: var(--font-ui); transition: background var(--motion-duration-state) var(--motion-easing-state), color var(--motion-duration-state) var(--motion-easing-state); } .ds-tab:hover { background: var(--color-surface-raised); color: var(--color-text); } .ds-tab:focus-visible { outline: var(--border-width-focus) solid var(--color-focus); outline-offset: var(--focus-offset); }

narrative.overview:
PenguinOps looks like the IT department it is set in. Admins label everything: switch ports, cables, servers, shelves, with printed label-maker tape, and they sort cables by colour so that anyone can see what a line is for. The game takes exactly these two habits as its visual system. Names and IDs that matter are printed on tape; each kind of work has its own cable colour; everything else is matte rack metal that stays quiet so the terminal can be the main stage.

The world lends the interface four things only: palette, type, density and one signature move. Layout, navigation and controls stay the familiar ones of a modern desktop game (ADR 0020): a top bar, a side panel with tabs, a large terminal and a key-hint footer. Someone who has played any coding game knows where everything is before they notice the tape.

The signature move: new tickets, mails, ranks and achievements print out as a strip of tape. It is the only thing that moves on its own.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, matte rack-metal ground with hairline rules; no glow, no gradients, no glass.
Label tape (yellow and white, black condensed caps) for ticket IDs, panel names, the rank and toasts.
Cable colours carry the kind of work: tickets, mail, handbook, incidents.
Fibre orange belongs to the player: their prompt, cursor and active ticket.
One grid: every size is a multiple of the terminal's character cell.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The tape strip prints out at the steady speed of a label maker (480 ms, linear). State changes on hover, focus and press answer within 120 ms with an exponential ease-out. Nothing else moves, and "reduce motion" sets both to zero.

rules.name: The Quarantine Rule
rules.body: Colour lives only on tape and cable runs. Grounds, panels and text stay neutral. If a colour appears somewhere else, it needs a meaning.

rules.name: The Fibre Rule
rules.body: Fibre orange marks only what the player is doing right now. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Scheme Rule
rules.body: Every colour is a semantic token named by its purpose, so the colour schemes of ROADMAP M3.9 (retro CRT, Solarized, high contrast) only swap values, pass the same contrast pairs and never require a screen change.

rules.name: The Pair Rule
rules.body: A new colour token comes with the pairs it appears in, or with the reason why it is decorative.

rules.name: The Real-Code Rule
rules.body: Monospace only for terminal output, commands, paths, file names and data, never as a "technical" costume for labels or headings.

rules.name: The Label Rule
rules.body: Tape type is set in caps and only on tape. Running text is never in caps.

rules.name: The Flat Rack Rule
rules.body: Panels sit flush like units in a rack. No card shadows, no glow, no nested cards.

dos: **Do** print ticket IDs, the product name, the rank and toast titles on tape.
**Do** give each kind of work its cable colour, consistently, on tabs, toasts and states.
**Do** keep fibre orange for the player's prompt, cursor and active ticket only.
**Do** build every screen from the tokens in `apps/ui/src/tokens.css`; a missing value becomes a new token, not a literal.
**Do** let the one motion be the tape printing out, and show it at once when "reduce motion" is on.
**Do** keep every control a standard, recognisable one: tabs, buttons, lists, inputs.
donts: **Don't** use the hacker cliché: green on black, matrix rain, neon glow, scanlines as the default look (scanlines stay an optional effect, ADR 0020).
**Don't** fall back to the category standard of charcoal rounded cards with one blue accent.
**Don't** put tape on running text, buttons or every row; tape is for names and IDs.
**Don't** use gradients, glass, glow or hard offset shadows.
**Don't** write a colour, a gap or a duration directly in a component.
**Don't** convey a state by colour alone; every cable colour comes with a label or icon.
